value.note: Single package option. Pins per the simplified schematic on p.1: VIN, SW, GND, VBST, EN, VFB.

source.ref: Description and Device Information, p.1; Pin Configuration and Functions, p.3

value.note: A buck converter, so unlike every LDO in this batch the input must be comfortably ABOVE the output. Note the 4.5 V floor: this part cannot run from a 3.3 V rail, and a nominal 5 V USB input sits only 0.5 V above the minimum. UVLO wakes at 3.8-4.3 V and shuts down at 3.3-3.4 V (Electrical Characteristics, p.6).

source.ref: §5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, p.4 — VIN supply input voltage range 4.5 to 17 V

value.note: Absolute maximum for VIN and EN. Only 2 V above the 17 V recommended maximum, so a 12 V rail with inductive transients needs care. The SW node has its own limits (-2 to 19 V, and -3.5 to 21 V for 10 ns transients) and VBST goes to 25 V, but VIN is the rail a topology check compares against.

source.ref: §5.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings, p.4 — input voltage VIN, EN -0.3 to 19 V

value.note: Adjustable via an external feedback divider, not a fixed-option part. Table 7-2 (p.15) gives the exact divider for each common output: R2 is always 10.0 kOhm and R1 is 3.09 / 3.74 / 5.76 / 9.53 / 13.7 / 22.6 / 33.2 / 54.9 / 75 kOhm for 1 / 1.05 / 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.8 / 2.5 / 3.3 / 5 / 6.5 V respectively. Those divider values are design data with no slot in this questionnaire, so they are recorded here rather than dropped.

source.ref: Features p.1 ('Output voltage range: 0.76V to 7V'); Table 7-2 Recommended Component Values, p.15

value.note: 3 A synchronous step-down converter. The current limit is separately specified as 3.3 / 4.2 / 5.1 A (min/typ/max) measured at VOUT = 1.05 V with L1 = 1.5 uH, so the guaranteed limit sits just above the 3 A rating. On-resistances are 95 mOhm high-side and 57 mOhm low-side. This is an order of magnitude more current than any LDO in this batch and, being a switcher, without the dissipation penalty.

source.ref: Description p.1 ('3A synchronous step-down converters'); §5.5 Electrical Characteristics current limit and MOSFET rows, p.6

value.note: Nominal, measured at VIN = 12 V, VOUT = 3.3 V, IOUT = 1 A. The frequency is not truly constant: this is a D-CAP2 constant-on-time architecture, and the TPS563201 variant uses pulse-skip (Eco-mode) at light load, so the switching frequency drops proportionally to load current below the conduction-mode boundary (§6.3.2, p.11). The TPS563208 sibling runs forced continuous conduction instead and holds frequency. Figures 5-7 and 5-8 (p.8) plot the variation against input voltage and output current.

source.ref: Features p.1 ('580kHz switching frequency'); §5.5 Electrical Characteristics Fsw row, p.6; §6.3.2 Pulse Skip Control, p.11

inductance.note: Table 7-2 gives a MIN / TYP / MAX inductance per output voltage, and the minimum rises with output voltage: 1.5 uH up to 1.8 V, 2.2 uH at 2.5-3.3 V, 3.3 uH at 5-6.5 V. The maximum is 4.7 uH throughout. The arms below carry the MINIMUM for each band, which is the value a design check must not go under; typicals are 2.2 / 2.2 / 3.3 uH respectively. TI is explicit about why these matter: the values place the loop's high-frequency zero so that phase margin stays adequate, so an arbitrary inductor is a stability problem and not merely a ripple trade-off.

isat.text: The inductor saturation current rating must be greater than the calculated peak current, and the RMS or heating current rating must be greater than the calculated RMS current (Equations 4-6). No fixed number can be asserted because both depend on VIN, VOUT, L and Fsw. For orientation, TI's own 3 A design example computes a 3.5 A peak and 3.01 A RMS and then selects a WE 74431122 rated 13 A peak / 9 A RMS — i.e. a large margin over the calculation.

source.ref: §7.2.2 design example, Equations 4-6 and inductor selection text, p.15

value.note: Inductance is conditional on output voltage; saturation current is a derived requirement rather than a fixed figure.

source.ref: Table 7-2 Recommended Component Values and §7.2.2 inductor selection, p.15

value.note: REQUIRED, not optional: 'The TPS563201 and TPS563208 require an input decoupling capacitor.' TI recommends a ceramic capacitor over 10 uF. A bulk capacitor may also be needed depending on the application. The capacitor voltage rating must exceed the maximum input voltage — with a 17 V input capability that means a 25 V part, and ceramic derating with DC bias must be accounted for on top.
OPTIONAL. An additional 0.1 uF capacitor (C3) from pin 3 to ground provides extra high-frequency filtering.

Recommended range 20 uF to 68 uF, listed as C8 + C9 in Table 7-2 for every output voltage — i.e. the range does not change with VOUT even though the inductance does. The D-CAP2 scheme supports both specialty-polymer and ultra-low-ESR ceramic capacitors. TI's example uses two 22 uF TDK C3216X5R0J226M parts with about 2 mOhm ESR each, and Equation 7 gives the required RMS current rating (0.286 A calculated in that example).
